summary:
selfoss is a self-hosted RSS reader, and no sign-in was needed. I saved 5 views, and each one replayed with a similarity score of 1.00:
1. newest-stream (/): the main reader. It has a dark sidebar with the Newest/Unread/Starred filters and colored tags, next to a list of articles showing tag badges, source, author and time, plus a thumbnail on the top article.
2. article-expanded (/ then click "Inclusive dark mode: designing for everyone"): an article opened inline, with its body in several columns and an action bar for Star, Mark as read, Open and share buttons. Opening it marks the article as read, and that happens again on every replay.
3. sources-list (/manage/sources): the sources settings page, with Add source, OPML import and export links. Each of the 22 feeds has Edit and More actions, and the failing Tin Can Podcast feed is outlined in red.
4. source-edit (/manage/sources then click the first "Edit"): the inline edit form for Tin Can Podcast, with Title, Tags, Filter, Type and URL fields, a red 404 fetch error, and Save/Cancel.
5. opml-import (/opml): a separate page for uploading an OPML file.
I left out the Unread and Starred streams, which use the same layout as Newest, and search results, which also look like the stream. I didn't capture the tag color-picker popover either, because the 5-view limit was used up.
